events.title: Battle of Bunker Hill
events.description: British forces under General William Howe defeated American colonial militia on Breed's Hill and Bunker Hill near Boston, though at the cost of over 1,000 British casualties.
events.significance: Early major battle of the American Revolutionary War that showed colonial militias could stand against the British army and hardened resolve on both sides.

events.title: Statue of Liberty Arrives in New York Harbor
events.description: The French ship Isère delivered the dismantled Statue of Liberty, a gift from France, in 350 pieces packed in 214 crates to New York Harbor.
events.significance: The arrival led to the statue's assembly on Bedloe's Island and its dedication in 1886, making it an enduring symbol of freedom and democracy and of welcome to immigrants.

events.title: Watergate Break-in
events.description: Five men connected to the Committee to Re-elect the President were arrested for breaking into the Democratic National Committee headquarters at the Watergate complex in Washington, D.C.
events.significance: The arrests began the Watergate scandal, which led to the resignation of President Richard Nixon in 1974 and reshaped public trust in government and investigative journalism.

events.title: O.J. Simpson Low-Speed Police Chase
events.description: Following the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman, O.J. Simpson fled in a white Ford Bronco on Los Angeles freeways in a slow-speed chase watched live by an estimated 95 million Americans.
events.significance: The chase and the subsequent trial became a landmark media event, influencing 24-hour news coverage, celebrity culture, and national discussions about race and justice.

events.title: East German Uprising
events.description: Workers in East Berlin began protesting increased work quotas, and the demonstrations spread across East Germany before being suppressed by Soviet tanks and troops.
events.significance: It was one of the first major popular uprisings against Soviet-backed rule in the Eastern Bloc, foreshadowing later revolts in Hungary, Czechoslovakia, and Poland.
